previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 70-year-old woman with a history of CAD s/p CABG, hypothyroidism, osteoporosis, and anxiety was admitted for generalized weakness, urinary frequency, and a nonproductive cough after starting a generic antibiotic. Initial evaluation revealed elevated WBC and lactate, but cultures were negative. She was treated with IV antibiotics initially, transitioned to oral ciprofloxacin for a presumed UTI. Her proximal muscle weakness, mild ptosis, and elevated inflammatory markers raised concern for a cryptogenic myopathy, though myasthenia gravis was not confirmed. Thyroid function was suboptimal, prompting an increase in levothyroxine from 100 to 112 mcg daily. She remained stable, with improving labs and no respiratory compromise. Discharged home with plans for outpatient neuromuscular neurology evaluation, continuation of ciprofloxacin, and follow-up on thyroid function.

FINDINGS:

There is diffuse demineralization of the osseous structures.  Mild loss of
height anteriorly of the T11 vertebral body is re- demonstrated.  Superior
endplate central depressions of T4 and T5 vertebral bodies are relatively
unchanged.  There are multilevel degenerative changes with disc space
narrowing and calcification.  No subluxation is visualized.  Diffuse
atherosclerotic calcification of the aorta is noted.  The patient is status
post median sternotomy and CABG.

Within the lumbar spine, compression deformity of the L2 and L4 vertebral
bodies are unchanged, with approximately 50% loss of height of the L2
vertebral body, and 40% loss of height of the L4 vertebral body.  No new
fracture is seen.  There is no subluxation.  Mild intervertebral disc space
narrowing is noted at L1-2, L2-3, and L3-4.  Diffuse atherosclerotic
calcification of the abdominal aorta is present.  The sacroiliac joints are
not diastatic.  Sacrum appears intact, though assessment is limited by
overlying bowel gas.

bodies.
